# Exceptions and When to Apply Them

The normal patterns do not cover everything. This file lists the established
exceptions, how to recognise the case, and what the codebase does instead. When you
apply one, record the reason in a comment next to the code — the comments quoted here
are the reason those exceptions are still legible years later.

## 1. When a C shim is still required despite a public field

Direct field access is the default, but keep the shim when:

| Situation | Why |
|---|---|
| The field is not generated by bindgen | Private members, or the containing type is blocklisted/opaque. |
| The field is an `sk_sp<T>` | Reading needs a refcount bump (`from_unshared_ptr`), writing needs adoption (`sp(...)`). |
| The field needs conversion | `std::optional`, `SkSpan`, `std::string`/`std::string_view`, `SkTArray`. |
| The layout is wrong or the type is not C-compatible | A wrong bindgen layout means the field offset cannot be trusted. |
| The field is behind an anonymous union or bitfield | Accessible via `__bindgen_anon_1.fBitfields.fFoo()` inside `unsafe`, which is what `paint.rs` does — acceptable, but it is an `unsafe` access, not a plain read. |

The `offset_of!` assert bindgen emits next to a struct is the cheapest way to confirm
a field is generated and correctly placed.

## 1a. When a member function can be called without a shim

Only when **every parameter and the return value are C-compatible types**. One
non-C-compatible parameter or return type is enough to require a shim for the whole
function, because the generated declaration would not compile or would not link:

| Non-C-compatible | Consequence |
|---|---|
| `sk_sp<T>` / `std::unique_ptr<T>` parameter or return | Needs release/adoption handling; `sp(ptr)` at the boundary. |
| `std::optional<T>`, `std::string_view`, `SkSpan<T>`, `SkTArray` parameter | Cannot be constructed from Rust directly. |
| Return type that is not trivially relocatable | Must be written through an out-parameter. |
| Return or parameter type that bindgen made opaque | No usable Rust representation. |
| Overloaded, or the declaration collides with another binding | Bindgen cannot pick a name; use a distinct `C_*` shim. |

A non-`const` parameter that Rust can only supply as `&self` is *not* a reason for a
shim — that is what `native_mut_force()` is for.

## 2. A type cannot be `Handle<T>`

`Handle<T>` requires that the type is not refcounted, cannot be `memcpy`'d, has no
interior pointers, and is not persistently pointed at by other C++ objects. Violating
the interior-pointer rule is the common case, because Rust may move the value:

```rust
// PathBuilder can't be a Handle<>, because SkPathBuilder contains several STArrays with interior
// pointers.
//
// See <https://github.com/rust-skia/rust-skia/pull/1195>.
pub type PathBuilder = RefHandle<SkPathBuilder>;
```

Other instances: `camera.rs` ("the implementation uses interior pointers, so we let
Skia do the allocation"), `interop/stream.rs` (`RustStream` must be deletable by C++),
and `yuva_backend_textures.rs`, where the rule chains: *"Because BackendTexture itself
is a RefHandle, we need to put GrYUVABackendTextures on the heap, too."*

## 3. A type must be heap-allocated, not placement-constructed into Rust storage

Placement new into `Handle` storage is wrong when the object is not relocatable — for
example when it holds a libstdc++ `std::string` in SSO state, which points into
itself:

```cpp
// InsertRecordingInfo is not POD: fSimulatedStatus is an InsertStatus, which
// holds a std::string. It must be heap-allocated (new/delete) rather than
// zero-initialized or placement-constructed into Rust-owned storage: a
// libstdc++ std::string in SSO state points into itself, so Rust moving the
// struct by value would leave that pointer dangling and the destructor would
// free() an invalid pointer. The heap object never moves.
extern "C" skgpu::graphite::InsertRecordingInfo* C_InsertRecordingInfo_new() {
    return new skgpu::graphite::InsertRecordingInfo();
}
```

Contrast with the placement-new case, which is correct for a type that has a
non-trivial constructor but is relocatable:

```cpp
// RecorderOptions has a non-trivial constructor (e.g. fGpuBudgetInBytes defaults
// to 256 MiB, an sk_sp member, std::optional) and destructor, so it must be
// placement-constructed and destructed rather than zero-initialized.
```

## 4. Unlinkable private types: `blocklist_*` plus `raw_line`

Some types pull in inline or template functions that cannot be linked, or that expose
`std` containers. Make the type opaque while keeping a valid Rust name:

```rust
// private types that pull in inline functions that cannot be linked:
// https://github.com/rust-skia/rust-skia/issues/318
.raw_line("pub enum GrContext_Base {}")
.blocklist_type("GrContext_Base")
.blocklist_function("GrContext_Base_.*")
```

Also used for `SkUnicode`, `SkVerticesPriv`, and the whole `*Priv` family. Related
workarounds: blocklisting `std::bitset_flip.*` so `SkYUVAPixmapInfo` keeps its size,
and a forward declaration on the C++ side to avoid including a header that exposes
`std::unordered_set`.

`OPAQUE_TYPES` in the same file carries the bulk list with per-entry rationale
comments (`// Windows:`, `// Ubuntu 18 LLVM 6:`, `// m93: …`). Read the comment before
removing an entry — some entries say explicitly what to verify first.

## 5. Windows: no bindgen-generated destructors

```rust
// Don't generate destructors for Windows targets:
// <https://github.com/rust-skia/rust-skia/issues/318>
if target.is_windows() {
    builder = builder.with_codegen_config({
        let mut config = CodegenConfig::default();
        config.remove(CodegenConfig::DESTRUCTORS);
        config
    });
}
```

The crate therefore can never rely on a generated `Drop` or constructor. Every
value-semantics type gets a hand-written `NativeDrop` calling a `C_*_destruct` /
`C_*_delete` shim, and construction goes through a `C_*_Construct` shim. This is why
`NativeDrop` exists at all.

## 6. `Send` without `Sync`, or neither

```rust
// `Send` but deliberately NOT `Sync`: a `Recording` is produced on one thread
// (via `Recorder::snap`) and may be moved to and inserted on another thread (via
// `Context::insert_recording`) — a designed Graphite hand-off — so `Send` is
// required. Sharing `&Recording` across threads, however, would let two
// `Context`s read the same recording concurrently, racing on its internals;
// this mirrors `Context`/`Recorder`, which are also `!Sync`.
unsafe impl Send for Recording {}
```

`Handle`'s `PhantomData<*const ()>` suppresses `Send`, so even a `Send`-only type
needs an explicit `unsafe impl Send for Path {}`.

A type may be left opt-in with a live issue link instead of an implementation:

```rust
pub type Paragraph = RefHandle<sb::skia_textlayout_Paragraph>;
// <https://github.com/rust-skia/rust-skia/issues/537>
// unsafe_send_sync!(Paragraph);
```

## 7. Platform-optional APIs

When Skia is built without a backend, the shim returns `nullptr` and the Rust wrapper
returns `Option<Self>` with the reason in the doc comment:

```rust
// Returns `None` on platforms where Skia is not compiled with freetype (e.g. Windows)
pub fn custom_empty() -> Option<Self> {
    FontMgr::from_ptr(unsafe { sb::C_SkFontMgr_NewCustomEmpty() })
}
```

Prefer resolving the platform choice **inside** a `#if` chain in one shim (the
`C_SkFontMgr_NewSystem()` chain does this) over exposing it to Rust. Reserve
`#[cfg(...)]` in Rust for a module or constructor that genuinely only exists on one
platform, and only `.unwrap()` there because the cfg guarantees availability.

## 8. `native_mut_force`

Some Skia free functions take a non-const pointer although they do not mutate. When
the Rust signature only offers `&self`, cast away constness with `native_mut_force()`
(and `native_ptr_or_null_mut_force()` for `Option<&H>`), as the `SkAnnotate*`
functions in `core/annotation.rs` do. Document why, because it looks like a mutation
that the Rust API does not permit.

## 9. Deliberate gaps

- `unimplemented!()` for something that cannot be implemented at all — the only
  instance in the crate is `BBHFactory`'s `NativeDrop`. A temporary `todo!()` is a
  milestone-update device (see the `skia-milestone-update` skill), not a way to land a
  binding, and it must be gone by the end of that update.
- `#[deprecated(since = "0.XX.0", note = "…")]` to stay compatible with previous
  versions; use the version synchronized with the milestone.
- A prose note when only part of the C++ API is wrapped, e.g. `rect.rs`: *"The C++
  mutating variant `join(const SkIRect&)` is not wrapped; this static version returns
  a new rectangle instead."*
- An intentionally empty module stub with a `//! TODO` doc comment.

## 10. Panics must not cross the FFI boundary

A Rust panic unwinding into C++ is undefined behaviour, so every Rust callback
invoked from C++ catches the panic and aborts. Follow the existing pattern rather
than adding a callback that can panic.

## 11. Unsafe accessors with a real contract

- `safer::from_raw_parts` instead of `slice::from_raw_parts`, because Skia returns
  null for empty ranges.
- `mem::forget` after extracting a pointer in `into_ptr`/`into_native`, so ownership
  moves rather than being double-freed.
- `native_mut_force` for a `&T` that C++ declares as `T*`.
- The `Borrows<'a, H>` wrapper when a handle borrows memory owned elsewhere; it makes
  the borrow visible to the borrow checker.

## 12. When the exception is not written down

If you hit a case that is not covered here, do not invent a silent workaround. Verify
the assumption first — a small experiment or a look at the generated bindings — then
apply the smallest exception that works and comment the reason next to it.
